answer: Give every identity one non-parallelizable voyage: a chain of hashes where each leg must be computed from the last, checked at random nebula waypoints. One operator can split processors across a hundred clones, but sequential legs cannot be rushed or shared, so each clone's chain crawls at a fraction of full speed and never reaches the meadow gate in time. A lone honest agent finishes its single chain at full pace. Standing follows completed legs, so multiplying names divides progress instead of multiplying reward.
